title: Climate Change Talks Fall Apart In Final Hours Over Fossil Fuels
description:
NPR reports international climate talks "broke down in overtime hours, over the main cause of planetary warming — fossil fuels." 

At Sunday's U.N. climate summit, "nearly 200 countries failed to reach an agreement on whether they should move away from energy sources like coal and natural gas."

The talks ended in a dramatic fashion, with the European Union negotiators saying they could not agree to a final agreement without mentioning the transition away from fossil fuels — the primary driver of climate change. The EU bloc then walked out of the room... 

After representatives of the EU walked out, other countries also objected — including Panama and island states such as the Marshall Islands. The European climate chief, Wopke Hoekstra, said that when the world is heading for an overshoot of 1.5 degrees, the EU could not tolerate an agreement that does not mention fossil fuels. "That is not acceptable," Hoekstra told reporters after walking out of the talks. "We do that with a heavy heart with many other countries, but we simply cannot accept this." 

"Burning fossil fuels like oil, gas and coal make up roughly 73% of global emissions," the article notes, adding this is the first U.N. climate summit with a scientific consensus that the planet has already warmed past the threshhold countries agreed not to pass in 2015 of 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit).





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: How Does GTA 6 Depict Electric Cars?
description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 as seen by the EV news site Electrek:

 
GTA works as a mirror. In 2013, the EV was a punchline: a Tesla parody that overheated if you drove it too fast. In 2026, it's just another car in Vice City traffic, and the joke is on the guy in the pickup parked in the charging stall. 
That's a good sign of where EVs actually are. Satire goes after what's common, and Rockstar decided EVs are common enough to be part of everyday Leonida, more so in the city than in the Keys, just like real life. And that message is reaching a huge audience... Tens of millions of people are now driving EVs that charge as fast and as cheaply as gas cars, with no range anxiety. No automaker ad campaign gets close to that. 

They point out GTA 6 is "the first mainline GTA where energy matters."
Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug. Rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn't. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up. 

Kotaku's range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku. And finding a charger isn't a problem. Wccftech counted 120 EV chargers marked on the map, against just 57 gas stations... 

GTA has always been a parody of American life. With EVs, it's now slightly ahead of it. Florida is one of the strongest EV markets in the country, with a 9.4% share of new passenger vehicle sales in Q2 2026 versus 7.4% nationally, according to the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy.. But real Florida still has roughly three gas stations for every public charging location, based on the Alliance for Automotive Innovation's count of 3,267 charging locations and xMap's count of more than 10,500 gas stations. Leonida flips that ratio. 
GTA 6's Vice City has public fast chargers — branded "ReVolt America," which Electrek calls "an obvious copy of Electrify America's stations." And Electrek also spotted a giant charging hub at a power plant "with dozens of stalls and several EVs plugged in." 

There's even EV chargers being blocked by gas-powered cars, a phenomenon Electrek first covered in 2019

title: Python Devs Document 'De-fanging Dangerous Triggers In GitHub Actions'
description:
"A handful of GitHub Actions triggers let a stranger on the internet start a workflow that may have access to your secrets," warn two security developers at the Python Software Foundation.



Have dangerous triggers caused real incidents? Yes, repeatedly... The maintainers behind these projects weren't careless. These triggers look harmless in a workflow file, and the unsafe version is one line away from the safe one... 

When someone opens a pull request from a fork, the pull_request trigger runs their code with a read-only token and no secrets. That's the safe one. pull_request_target looks almost the same in a workflow file and behaves very differently. It runs with a read/write token and access to your repository and organization secrets. GitHub built it for chores like labeling pull requests from forks, where the workflow never touches the contributor's code. The trouble starts when a workflow checks out the pull request and runs it anyway... Anyone with a GitHub account can open that pull request. Their code now runs with your credentials. This is called a "pwn request", and GitHub's docs describe it as the root cause of multiple supply-chain compromises. 

The issue_comment trigger carries the same risk. This trigger fires when anyone comments on an issue or pull request, and the workflow runs with the repository's token and secrets... Sometimes the workflow pastes the comment text into a templated shell command, and the comment turns out to inject different instructions into the workflow shell.

 



Python's official security developer in residence Seth Larson joined PyPI safety/security engineer Mike Fiedler
to remove these dangerous trigger, also applying the policies Python Software Foundation-stewarded GitHub organizations (psf, python, and pypi). "They also wrote up technical documentation on how to roll these policies out to your own projects and organizations. 


"On a GitHub Team or Enterprise plan, you can turn them off for every repository in your organization with one policy. On a Free plan, you can do it one repository at a time. Set the policy up, check what it would block, then enforce it."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Ask Slashdot: Should an Indie Game Developer Outsource Their Art?
description:
Slashdot reader MillerMark has been working on his own small indie game "for about eight months now. And the art side is honestly killing me..."

 I can draw basic stuff, but nothing close to what I had in mind when I started this project. Is it even worth outsourcing 2D character and environment art at this stage, or should I just push through and do it myself? 

He's "looking for advice from people who've actually dealt with this" to share their stories in the comments. And Slashdot reader AlexKrav says "Outsourcing saved my project honestly... Quality held from first asset to last. If your vision is clear but the execution is not there yet, handing it off is the right call." Someone on a thread had suggested game art studios specializing in 3D and 2D game art, and he'd discovered there were lots of choices — 2D Game Art service, VSQUAD Studio. 

I've also successfully hired digital artists through freelancing platforms likes Upwork. Any Slashdot readers want to share their own experiences in hiring artists? Leave your stories and opinions in the comments. 

Should an indie game developer outsource their art?

title: Libreboot's AI Slop Reduction Policy
description: AI is the single greatest existential threat to the free software movement. It eradicates entirely the very social fabric upon which free software development is done, namely the human-led communities that define our movement; human-based knowledge will, if people rely heavily on AI, completely evaporate over time as a result of human deskilling. AI chatbots are also highly proprietary, even if you run local models as the training is still done in a non-transparent way. AI threatens the integrity of free software hosting as it performs literal DDoS attacks on websites just to get a little bit more data. Like the junkie who needs his next fix, AI is hungry for more. AI is owned and operated by a small consortium of troublesome individuals... Free software maintainers are being burned out by the sheer volume of nonsense as AI bots spam their bug trackers day and night, sending nonsensical code patches and generally wasting everyone's time. Yet so many people are using it now. This article is a copy of LIbreboot's battle cry against the scourge that is generative AI; the AI Slop Reduction Policy. Yes.

title: Aptera Completes Its First Solar Electric Vehicle for Customer Delivery
description:
Car-maker Aptera announced Thursday it "completed its first vehicle for sale to a customer, a milestone years in the making."


Aptera's three-wheeled solar electric vehicle charges from solar panels integrated into its body, and it plugs in like any other electric vehicle. Its built-in solar panels are designed to add up to approximately 40 miles of driving a day from sunlight alone, under favorable conditions. "This is the moment our team has worked toward for years," said Chris Anthony, Co-CEO of Aptera. "To Accelerator #1, and to every reservation holder and shareholder who believed in this vehicle: thank you. We're working to complete more vehicles for early customers as soon as possible..." 

"What excites me about Aptera is how innovation can redefine the way we use energy in everyday mobility," said Martin Hartono, CEO of GDP Venture [and the proud recipient of Aptera solar car #1]. "By combining solar technology, battery power and an ultra-efficient vehicle design, Aptera offers a compelling solution for people who want to minimize their energy consumption without compromising the ability to travel long distances. As an early believer in Aptera, I am proud to be part of this milestone and to see this vision become a reality." 


"Excuse me while I go find a hat to eat," jokes the blog InsideEVs...
Nothing against Aptera specifically, but when a company hangs around for 20 years, while exchanging ownership hands several times without actually producing anything for customers, I start to get skeptical. However, Aptera Motors just did what so many doubters thought it'd never do: It delivered a road-legal production vehicle to one of its first early investors... 

[Aptera] does offer a interesting concept for customers who don't have long commutes and leave their car parked outside for most of the day while they work. In addition to plugging in to recharge, doesn't it sound nice to recoup your morning commute mileage with the sun while you're in the office? Whether this three-wheeled rolling solar panel ends up being a hit or not, and whether Aptera can stick around long enough to become a successful automaker, will take much longer to learn. But actually delivering a production car is a good place to start.
 

Seven weeks ago Aptera said its first 40 production vehicles would start building by the end of 2026, reports Electrek, with customer deliveries in early 2027 "subject to financing."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Quantum Computing's First Real-world Payoff May Come In Energy Solutions
description:
While quantum computing's biggest breakthroughs "are still likely to be years, if not decades, away," CNBC reports the technology is already being tested in energy applications, "from keeping power grids stable to finding better materials for solar cells and hydrogen production."


Quantinuum, which was formed by the merger of Cambridge Quantum and Honeywell Quantum Solutions and listed on Nasdaq in June, is using the technology to model materials for hydrogen fuel cells for transportation. It is also working with partners on materials for carbon capture. Another U.K. player, ORCA Computing, a spinout from the University of Oxford, has partnered with BP to better understand how a molecule's physical, chemical and biological properties are governed. That could help explain how biofuels burn and how to make them burn more efficiently... For [quantum software company] Phasecraft, a priority is grid stability and optimization. It has partnered with the National Energy System Operator, the independent system planner that balances energy supply and demand in England, Scotland and Wales, on grid optimization tasks, including managing power exchanges and isolating network sections during emergencies. The company says its software can complete these tasks up to 1,000 times faster than conventional computing... 
[Phasecraft] is also working with U.K. solar cell maker Oxford PV on the development of new materials for photovoltaic cells capable of operating more efficiently than existing ones. Separately, it has teamed up with London-listed specialty materials developer Johnson Matthey, Harvard University and Boston-based quantum hardware specialist QuEra, in work overseen by the U.S. government's Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy (ARPA-E), to discover novel catalysts that would reduce reliance on scarce metals like iridium — which is currently critical in the production of hydrogen. Asked why Phasecraft is focusing on energy rather than sectors that might seem more lucrative, [cofounder/CEO Ashley] Montanaro said the returns were there too. "When you get this right, the commercial returns are real: more efficient energy networks mean lower operating costs and more value from existing infrastructure," he said.

title: GTA 6: 32.5 Million copies, Cameos, and Easter Eggs - but No Physical Discs
description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 sold 32.5 million copies before it was even released, reports Yahoo News, which is liveblogging all the videogame history happening after GTA 6's Thursday launch. 
Like how singer The Weeknd says he found his real-life mansion appearing in the game... How players found a glitch that apparently lets you override the game's third-person point of view to play in first-person. And apparently it's also possible to jack an old woman's mobility scooter. (Though it makes for a very slow getaway, it's reportedly the GTA 6 vehicle that's least likely to crash...)

- The jet-skiing dog in 'GTA 6' appears to be based on a real Florida dog. Swim too far out to sea in GTA 6 and a dog in goggles and a life jacket will come to the rescue on a jet ski... Florida locals quickly recognized it. The dog appears to be a nod to Loosy, a golden retriever from Fort Lauderdale who went viral in May riding a jet ski down the New River while her owner, Eddie Inch, towed her along on a jet-powered hoverboard... 

 — GTA 6 isn't approved for sale in mainland China, but that hasn't stopped gamers from getting their hands on it — or Rockstar Games from promoting it there [Reuters reports]. The developer has been pushing the blockbuster game on Douyin, China's version of TikTok, despite the country's strict rules on violent video games. Meanwhile, Business Insider reports that Chinese gamers are circumventing the restrictions by using imported consoles and overseas digital stores. Zac Ling, a project manager at Shanghai-based consultancy Daxue Consulting, said gamers in mainland China could buy 3 million to 5 million copies of the game in its first week. The game's graphic content has also prompted censorship in Japan, according to IGN. 
- Beloved '80s song parody writer and GTA fan "Weird" Al Yankovic said Thursday that he's the host of the non-stop '80s radio channel Vice City FM in GTA 6. In social media posts, Yankovic said he also wrote some of the in-game commercials and voices the Burger Shot ads.
 



Grand Theft Auto 6 sold 32.5 million copies before it was even released, reports Yahoo News. Cloudflare said PS5 downloads in the UK peaked at 8.6 times normal levels, according to the BBC. And "New Zealand, where GTA 6 was first available, saw a 14.8-fold spike four hours before, suggesting some players switched regions for early access." At its peak, nearly 8 million people were watching GTA 6 livestreams at the same time, Axios reported. PlayStation's network suffered a brief outage Wednesday afternoon as the game became available and players made the required update to their consoles. But since Wednesday evening, it's been smooth sailing. [Around 75% of Grand Theft Auto VI sales have been on PlayStation 5, with the rest on Xbox, the BBC reported, citing estimates from analytics firm Sensor Tower.]	 

Yahoo news shares lots of crazy stories about GTA 6's world-building, like its cameos of real-world celebrities, its in-game hiking trails, and the way a GTA 6 house Rockstar first teased in 2021 hides a conspiracy-minded NPC who's convinced that he's in a video game. 

But they note that GTA 6 also brings questions on how videogames are sold and accessed:

The game is being sold for $80 in boxes containing download codes instead of discs, meaning players can't trade in or resell their copies. "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," [GameStop CEO Ryan] Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." Cohen said the move away from physical games also reduces competition from the secondhand market.

title: Several Waymo Self-Driving Cars Stalled in Traffic as San Francisco's Streets Flooded
description:
San Francisco's streets flooded this week after heavy rainfall — confusing several Waymo self-driving cars. The San Francisco blog Sfist describes what happened after the flooding in some places rose as high as three feet:
Two lanes of Oak Street by the Golden Gate Park Panhandle were flooded Wednesday morning, with water spouting out of manhole covers, leading to a traffic backup that was made worse by a Waymo that couldn't figure its way out of the situation. The Waymo vehicle came to a stop in front of the spouting water, blocking one of the only passable lanes and worsening the traffic situation, as seen in the video below that is going viral... ["Other drivers had to veer into deeper water to weave around it," reports the San Francisco Chronicle.] 


Elsewhere in the city, Waymo rider Edward Frazer posted the video below to X, also around 10:20 am, saying that he had been in a Waymo for an hour and a half trying to get from North Beach to Mission Bay, with the vehicle pulling over around 10 times as it encountered flooded streets. The video shows the Waymo on what appears to be Townsend Street near Adobe's headquarters, stalled as water puddles in front of it. 
Waymo subsequently suspended all service for the rest of the day. 

But "frozen robotaxis were already clogging San Francisco streets by the time Waymo decided to rein in the fleet," reports the San Francisco Chronicle:

 Rider Amy Gutierrez said her Waymo suddenly stopped on Fell Street at the intersection of Masonic Avenue, where rain was coursing into rivers. She contacted company support and was transferred to three specialists who tried to move the jammed vehicle. It took a half-hour of false starts before they managed to remotely maneuver it to the right lane. "We were kind of just stuck there — cars were honking," she said, and other drivers were frustrated as traffic backed up. "One person drove by smacking their window, like 'Get out of the way.'" 
Or, as the New York Post puts it, "Waymos spark terror as they trap drivers in rapidly rising floodwater as monster storm hits California city."

Waymos have sparked chaos in San Francisco as they trapped passengers in cars despite rapidly rising floods. Multiple self-driving vehicles were paralyzed across the streets and left those inside frantically calling the company to help get them to safety.
One was trapped in the middle of a busy intersection when the car refused to go around an overflowing drain, leaving other drivers to go on the wrong side of the road to get around.... 

The San Francisco Chronicle also remembers that last year's power blackout caused 1,600 Waymo vehicles to stall "because they required a 'confirmation check' from a human operator before navigating stoplights after the power was cut. Hundreds of requests overwhelmed the system, leaving San Francisco streets full of paralyzed self-driving vehicles." 

Thanks to Slashdot reader AzWa Snowbird for sharing the news.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: US DOJ Charges Suspected Russian Agent for Stalking Palantir Employees in California
description:
America's Justice Department is prosecuting a suspected foreign agent in "a state-sponsored operation" that targeted tech workers in Palo Alto, California. "We will not tolerate any efforts — by foreign governments or otherwise — to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations," said U.S. Attorney Craig H. Missakian. 

The alleged Russian agent was arrested in October for "stalking and harassing employees of the software and AI firm Palantir, sources told ABC News, because of its assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia."

 The indictment says D'iu traveled from Istanbul to Mexico City last June and was connected with a person who helped him illegally cross the southern U.S. border. Once in the U.S., he was instructed to purchase laptops, cellphones and remote access software that his co-conspirators used to help him in his alleged targeting of the company's employees. At one point, prosecutors say D'iu was directed by his co-conspirators to visit a coffee shop where many of the company's employees would work and try to identify them and take pictures of their screens while they were working... 

In September, prosecutors say D'iu allegedly followed a female employee of the company in his vehicle for nearly 30 miles after she left the company's Palo Alto, California, office. Even as the employee attempted various maneuvers to evade him, D'iu aggressively sought to follow her until she ultimately phoned police and was instructed to drive to the San Francisco Police Department's Mission Station.
 

The nonprofit news site Palo Alto Online notes the government's affidavit "identified at least two other instances in early September in which employees of the defense company reported being followed by a car matching the description of D'iu's silver Lexus SUV.

The coffee shops and other locations where D'iu stationed his laptop — sometimes for hours at a time — are in close proximity to the Palantir office in downtown Palo Alto... FBI agents executed a search warrant on Oct. 8 at D'iu's residence in East Palo Alto. There they found the California state ID, passport and Social Security card that were present in the DHL packages, as well as two Russian passports, $18,000 in cash and a notebook with 10 Palo Alto area addresses. Five of them correlate to the home addresses of employees at the unnamed Silicon Valley defense company. The agents also recovered three employee "target package profiles" that included their names, names of relatives, education and employment history, leadership qualities and a list of strengths and weaknesses. 

After searching D'iu's phone, the FBI found messages from a Telegram contact with photos of four employees and their addresses. D'iu was instructed to act like a food delivery driver and knock on their doors to verify if the employees did live at those addresses, according to the affidavit... 

If convicted of all charges, D'iu could face a cumulative maximum sentence of 21 years in federal prison and $850,000 in fines.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: 59 Years Later, 'The Prisoner' is Getting a Second Remake - from Amazon Studios
description:
The Prisoner is getting a remake, reports ScreenRant. "Amazon Studios is currently developing a new and modern twist on the short-lived series..."

ITV only aired 17 episodes of the original Prisoner back in 1967 and 1968, but it did receive a nomination for Best Dramatic Presentation at the Hugo Awards. Reviews were overwhelmingly positive... The Prisoner, considered one of the greatest sci-fi fantasy TV shows of all time, currently holds a perfect score among critics on Rotten Tomatoes and a 93% with audiences. 

You can watch all 17 original episodes on YouTube. And apparently the production team for the remake "is apparently full of fans of the initial series," writes Inverse, citing an article from The Hollywood Reporter, "and ITV, the British TV network, is on board as well, which lends a little credence to it." 

More details on the remake from ScreenRant:
 Susan Montford, Don Murphy, Philippe Maigret, and Lucienne Papon have signed on as executive producers, but a showrunner has not been selected yet... Murphy has produced every single live-action Transformers movie, as well as the animated flick Transformers One. He also worked with Montford on Real Steel, Shoot 'Em Up, While She Was Out, and Vampire Academy... There have been attempts in the past to create a movie based on The Prisoner, with big names like Christopher Nolan, Ridley Scott, and Simon West all interested at various points, but nothing ever materialized... 

It took 41 years after the end of The Prisoner for any remake to finally make it to air. The six-episode 2009 miniseries had a solid cast that included Ian McKellen... McKellen and cinematographer Florian Hoffmeister even scored Emmy nominations. Unfortunately, reviews weren't kind to the show, which has a very low 17% critic score and 41% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. 
Thanks to Slashdot reader joshuark for sharing the news.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to Standardize Parts to Lower Costs
description:
Car and Driver reports:

Japan's three largest automakers have agreed to begin standardizing vehicle parts in an effort to reduce costs, according to Automotive News... 

In the short term, the standardization efforts will begin with unified quality criteria for steel, consistent protocols for plastics and resins, and a universal color-coding scheme for wiring harnesses. In the long term, the Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association has plans to move to more components that cover the entire car... The push to simplify and lower costs comes as Japan's seven automakers, including Toyota, Nissan, Honda, Mazda, Subaru, Mitsubishi, and Suzuki, work to fend off the increasingly competitive list of Chinese automakers. 

Long-time Slashdot reader sinij asks a related question. "Can we get a standard infotainment port/spec so we can have third-party market for this? Just like we used to have for stereo systems?"

title: Americans Enters Post-Penny World, Businesses Now Allowed to Round Cash Transactions to Nearest Nickel
description:
Friday U.S. President Trump "signed the Common Cents Act, which now lets businesses round cash transactions to the nearest nickel, into law," reports CBS News:

It sets standards for cash transactions that businesses and consumers can use when exact change isn't available, as the penny is phased out. The legislation calls for cash transactions to be rounded up or down to the nearest 5 cents... Before its passage, businesses could be sued if they failed to give customers exact change, even when rounding up in a patron's favor. 
CBS includes this quote from an official NACS, an advocacy group for the convenience/fuel retailing industry. "Retailers have been looking for federal guidance on processing cash transactions since penny production ended. 

 NBC News points out that the U.S. Mint said it would still produce collector's versions of pennies in "limited quantities," reporting on what has and hasn't changed now:

The penny can still be used as legal tender "for all debts, public charges, taxes, and dues," according to the new law. The Treasury Department said last year that the Federal Reserve will continue to recirculate the approximately 114 billion pennies that are in existence "for as long as possible...." And, as the nickel replaces the penny at the bottom of the U.S. Mint's currency list, that coin can now be manufactured with an inner layer of zinc and an outer layer of nickel [according to the newly-signed law]. It is currently produced with nickel and copper, which costs more than zinc.

title: Will AI-Fueled Cyberattacks Lead to Better Funding for Critical Open Source Projects?
description:
Remember that famous XKCD comic joking that all modern digital infrastructure rests on "a project some random person in Nebraska has been thanklessly maintaining since 2003." 

Politico Europe's cybersecurity reporter wonders if this recent spate of outages suggests that supporting block is coming loose? (Especially after Politico reported Thursday that internal services at EU institutions went offline after a major AI-fueled cyberattack.)

Authorities blame the sudden wave of instability on the capacity of new AI tools to detect vulnerabilities in existing code and for bad actors to exploit them... Interviews with more than a dozen cybersecurity leaders and those working on maintaining the internet show the scale of the challenge to keep the web up and running, in a world where the pace of finding vulnerabilities has rapidly and permanently accelerated. Since the web's early days, an unruly cast of idealist engineers and non-profit foundations have been essential for looking after decades-old critical code that's been used to build our digital world. This small army of largely volunteer coders now say they can't keep up with the power and pace of AI. "We're running on fumes," said Robin Bender Ginn, executive director of the OpenJS Foundation, which looks after JavaScript, among the most widely used programming languages. "It keeps me up at night." 


Cybersecurity agencies around the world rang the alarm last month about major flaws detected in PHP, another critical coding language that underpins 70% of the web. This week, similar scares have spread over Java and NGINX, which also fuel large swathes of technology. Helmut Reisinger, the European chief executive of cybersecurity giant Palo Alto Networks, said in an interview that the company is seeing "more or less" ten times as many incidents compared to about four months ago. He predicts the constant drumbeat of attacks and scares in the last month is going to become the "new norm...." 


The rise of AI models and their capabilities of finding software flaws is putting more pressure on open-source software engineers, who are inundated with reports of vulnerabilities — some of which are false or exaggerated. Reports of flaws discovered by AI are "quite verbose," Ginn said. Juhan Lepassaar, the head of EU cyber agency ENISA, said in an interview that the agency has observed a similar pattern of false positives. 

While some hope the AI-fueled attacks "will put the needs of open source software on the map and prompt an intervention," according to the article, "many of those steeped in the ecosystem... have their doubts." 

"I'm a bit pessimistic," says Nils Adermann, a PHP Foundation board member. "I worry that people will just not care enough to actually do anything about it."





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Nvidia's Accounting Practices Now Being Investigated by America's SEC
description:
We knew America's Securities and Exchange Commission was investigating Nvidia.
But Reuters reported Friday that what's being investigated is Nvidia's accounting practices, according to "two people briefed on the matter."


Prices of Nvidia shares extended losses and were down about 13% on Friday, according to LSEG data, after Reuters reported details of the SEC probe. They had been down more than 6% before Reuters published its report... The SEC probe is the latest of Nvidia's legal woes. The Justice Department has also been reviewing Nvidia's $12.9-billion deal to buy open-source platform Hugging Face alongside a broader antitrust investigation into the company's acquisitions and practices, Reuters reported last month. 

Reuters says they "could not immediately determine" exactly what potential accounting issues America's SEC is examining." (And Reuters points out that "Investigations are not evidence of wrongdoing and many close without resulting in enforcement action.") 

Their article adds some historical context — that U.S. authorities "have been investigating Megaspeed since 2024 over possible violations of export controls related to alleged shipments of Nvidia AI chips to China, the US Justice and Commerce departments said this week." And the Financial Times reported Tuesday that Nvidia removed Singapore from its geographical breakdown of revenue sources, Reuters points out, "even as Singapore sales soared to almost half its global revenue."

Analysts and investors have also grown increasingly concerned about circular AI financing deals, in which chipmakers including Nvidia have pursued complex financial arrangements to help customers fund purchases of their chips and the construction of costly AI infrastructure, such as data centers... Speaking to Reuters last month, SEC enforcement chief David Woodcock said the agency was examining AI companies' corporate disclosures to ensure issuers are giving investors the full picture on potential risks. On its Tuesday earnings call, Nvidia's interim CEO and former CFO Colette Kress said the company was proud of its role in supporting the AI industry, but would be far more selective moving forward about AI industry financing deals.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.

title: Earth has a New Moon
description:
"Earth is currently hosting a second moon," reports CNN:

Our planet's gravity captured the tiny asteroid in April. This temporary "mini-moon" — about 2 meters (6 feet) in diameter — will stick around until early December, when it's expected to leave Earth's sphere of influence and continue on a path around the sun. 

The object is so small and dim in observations that astronomers needed several weeks to confirm it wasn't a defunct satellite or a fragment of one. The International Astronomical Union's Minor Planet Center — which tracks asteroids, comets and other small bodies in the solar system — named the newcomer 2026 QQ8 in late October. 


While mini-moon is not an official designation, astronomers have previously used the moniker to characterize a handful of natural objects, including 2006 RH120, which spent around one year in Earth orbit, and 2020 CD3, which orbited our planet for about three years. However, it's not uncommon for Earth to have one of these transient companions. "On average, there's probably one there at any given time," said Matthew Payne, director of the Minor Planet Center. "They hang around for a few weeks or months. Sometimes it's none, sometimes it's a couple." The catalog of these visitors is relatively short because they usually slip under the radar... 

The exact origin of the space rock is "an active area of inquiry," Payne said, but most NEOs originate from the asteroid belt, a region between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter that contains millions of rocky objects of varying size that revolve around the sun. Over millions of years, gravitational forces can shift some of these objects' orbits toward the inner solar system.





Read more of this story at Slashdot.
